descriptive_scope_notes: All outcomes use 0–1 coding with higher values indicating more government responsibility. Immigration-stock variables are country-level percent of population; migration flow is a distinct annual rate and will not be put on a common effect scale with stock. Initial modeling scope will use respondent-level OLS with basic demographics and wave indicators, report item-specific effects, and use country-clustered uncertainty because exposure varies by country-wave and countries recur across waves. Alternative exposure measures, controls and sample windows will be examined. No published findings or external research data will be used.

choice: Freeze p_d40f62 as the lead specification for the brief and reproducible final program.
reason: Among the six core responsibility items, unemployed support has the clearest negative estimate. The combined-stock model uses the broadest pooled complete-case sample (124,450 respondents, 38 countries, 92 country-waves); World Bank and UN stock alternatives give similar estimates. Flow, extra-control, single-wave and country-fixed-effect checks qualify the interpretation, so the brief will present this as a pooled cross-national association and foreground that it is not robust to country fixed effects. Other core outcome paths and exposure/control alternatives were considered.

rationale: Selected as the lead pooled cross-national estimate for support for government responsibility to the unemployed. It uses the combined stock series and the widest complete-case sample among the evaluated baseline and exposure alternatives (124,450 respondents; 38 countries; 92 country-waves), adjusts for age, sex, employment and wave, and has a negative estimate whose nominal 95% interval excludes zero. The World Bank and UN stock reruns support a similar direction, while the country-fixed-effects, added-controls, single-wave and annual-flow results show that the finding is sensitive to specification and should be framed as an observational between-country association. The nominal significance is not robust to a six-outcome Holm adjustment.
